chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abi ʿAbdillah ibn Salih, who said:

I had gone out in one year of the years in Baghdad. So I sought permission regarding departure, but permission was not granted to me. Thus I remained for twenty-two days, while the caravan had already departed to al-Nahrawan.

Then permission was granted to me to depart on Wednesday, and it was said to me: 'Depart on that day.' So I departed while despairing of catching up to the caravan, but I reached al-Nahrawan while the caravan was still there.
Then it was only that I fed my camels something before the caravan set out, so I set out as well. And he had supplicated for my safety, so I encountered no harm, and all praise is due to Allah.

key_terms.آيِسٌ: despairing or having lost hope of catching the caravan
key_terms.النَّهْرَوَانِ: al-Nahrawan, the destination or waypoint mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْخُرُوجِ: departure or setting out on a journey
key_terms.الْقَافِلَةُ: the traveling caravan being joined on the route
key_terms.بِالسَّلَامَةِ: for safety and protection from harm
key_terms.دَعَا: he supplicated in prayer on the narrator’s behalf
key_terms.سُوءًا: harm, evil, or misfortune encountered on the journey

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the benefit of seeking the Imam’s permission and du'a before travel?
ai.summary: This report recounts a travel incident in which departure was delayed until permission was granted, after which the narrator unexpectedly caught up with the caravan. It highlights the benefit of obedience to the Imam عليه السلام and the blessing of his du'a for safety during travel.
